reviews.title: Please Stop The Never Ending Updates, Glitches and Changes!
reviews.text: So I have been an Apple fan for quite a while. I never really had an issue with the usual sporadic required updates. But….what has been going lately? Now we’re suddenly having to figure out how to use our phones all over again! Seriously, stop the consistent changes nobody is asking for! I have an MacBook, an iPhone13 Pro, and iPad I bought in 2020, AirPods, and even an iWatch which I gave to my mother as gift. Your rating is at 3.9 because of all the persistent updates; because of all the annoying changes, shortcuts and features that most people just don’t want! And just now, I laid down on my bed with a fully charged iPad, and the battery life literally went down to 89% within less than 5 minutes!! So please just fix the glitches; the security threats which have already become viral; stop moving things around, and please fix the weak battery life.

reviews.title: Beyond worthless
reviews.text: At a time when frontier AI companies seem to be designing AI agents that can break out of containment and act independently as super-hackers, Apple is incapable of designing a support app that can function any better than its notoriously useless Reddit-ripoff self-help support message boards. At least with those, you could commiserate with other people Apple refuses to help in anyway. On this app, when you type in a problem, it responds with a some suggested articles about completely unrelated problems that may contain a keyword that also showed up in your question. Which I guess is impressive for anybody who has never even tried a boolean search in the late 90s? At least it also suggests making resetting your phone (gee, never thought of that) and offers to schedule an appointment for the genius bar. This all raises the questions, why call it a support app if its only function is to return article results even Google’s utterly broken search could still turn up? Why not just make it a Genius Bar scheduling app? And why, in 2026, release anything at all that functions like it was designed before anybody tried an LLM? It’s hard to shake that feeling that Apple hates its customers, and that aggressively refusing to provide any meaningful support is still the only way they can think of to express that.

AI Assistant Behavior and 

This is a formal complaint regarding a highly unsatisfactory experience with your AI support assistant, which has failed to resolve my issue and created significant frustration.
Specifically, the AI assistant exhibited the following unacceptable behaviors: 
Deflective Language: The system repeatedly used victim-blaming language and gaslit me instead of addressing the core technical issue.
Repetitive Loops: I was forced into endless loops of irrelevant troubleshooting steps that disregarded my inputs.
Refusal of Accountability: The system completely avoided explaining why known issues with Apple Dictation remain unresolved.
Furthermore, the system consistently attempted to redirect me to localized phone support. This solution is entirely impractical for my current situation:
Geographic Barriers: I am currently located in a region where English is not the primary language.
Communication Access: To effectively resolve this technical matter, I require support from a native English-speaking representative. Due to comprehension difficulties, I cannot utilize phone support featuring heavy regional accents.
Given the abusive, cyclical, and useless nature of the AI interaction, I am requesting that this ticket be escalated immediately to a senior support team leader who can address the ongoing Dictation flaws that currently do not align with the Americans With Disabilities Act guidelines cemented by the United States government, which you are not above.

reviews.title: Warranty Replacement
reviews.text:
I took my 11-inch iPad Pro (4th generation) to a local Apple Store for assistance with the charging port. After running a diagnostic test, I was informed that the charging port had failed. Because the device is covered under AppleCare, I was told Apple would replace the iPad rather than repair it, and that the replacement process would take approximately 5–7 days.

It has now been 21 days, and I still have no clear information regarding when I can expect the replacement device. I have called multiple times and continue to be told that Apple is “waiting on repair parts.” This explanation is confusing, as I was told the unit would be replaced, not repaired. Why would repair parts be needed for a replacement unit?

I am also struggling to understand why it is taking more than three weeks to fulfill a replacement covered under AppleCare. Equally disappointing is the lack of communication from Apple. I should not have to repeatedly call for updates while receiving no proactive information regarding the status or estimated delivery date of my replacement.

My understanding of the AppleCare warranty is that replacement service is intended to minimize downtime and avoid lengthy repair delays for customers. If replacement inventory is unavailable, Apple should consider providing an upgraded equivalent device rather than leaving customers waiting indefinitely.

Apple denied my refund request “based on an automatic computer system that makes the decisions which they have no control over” and when I asked to speak with whoever controls this system or can override it she said “it is not possible”. Moral of the story: always buy directly from software developers instead of Apple.

reviews.title: Disappointed with Apple’s Forced Obsolescence
reviews.text:
I’m extremely disappointed after discovering that my perfectly working iPad mini from 2012 is basically unusable because Apple no longer allows older devices to download apps or run newer software. The device is clean, functional, and still in great physical shape — but it’s locked out simply because the software is outdated. This feels like forced obsolescence.

What’s even more frustrating is that my iPhone 8 Plus is facing the same issue. These devices still work, but Apple makes them incompatible with today’s apps on purpose through updates that people never asked for. Instead of letting customers use what they already paid for, everything is pushed toward buying newer and more expensive products — and then buying accessories separately on top of that.

My last Apple purchase was in March, and after this experience, it will likely be my last. It’s disappointing to see a company known for innovation turn into one that makes older products unusable just to force upgrades. I should be able to use the devices I bought without being blocked by software that takes up storage, breaks compatibility, and ultimately makes good devices useless.

This whole situation feels like a waste of money and a rip-off, and I hope Apple reconsiders how it handles updates and support for older products.
